newsitem.title: USA: Emerging debt tracks U.S. Treasuries higher.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt tracks U.S. Treasuries higher.

text.p: Emerging debt prices ended the New York trading session higher across the board in light volume, boosted by a firmer U.S. Treasury market, traders said.
Spreads on emerging debt prices were quoted tighter by about five to ten basis points, they added.
"We've had a little bit of a relief rally late in the trading day boosted by a stronger U.S. Treasury market," said one Brady trader.
In the U.S.government market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was quoted up 20/32 at 94-16/32 to yield 7.07 percent at the close, versus 7.12 percent at Friday's close.
"We've definitely recovered in the U.S. market. After trading in a a tight range earlier we've moved to the upside," another trader said.
Brazil C bonds were up 5/8 at 75-3/8, Brazil Pars traded up 5/8 to 70-3/4 bid.
Mexico Pars rose 5/8 to 70-3/4 bid and Venezuela Pars gained 3/4 to trade at 70-1/2 bid.
Despite the improved tone in the marketplace volume remained light with very little client buying or selling seen, traders said.
"Today trading was characterized by short-covering and bottom-fishing...volume has been very light," said one Brady trader.
Another trader echoed the view, "We haven't seen much buying. I think it's the Street just repositioning itself."

Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez told Reuters Financial Television in Tokyo on Monday that domestic interest rates may move lower in the near-term following last week's move by Standard & Poor's to raise Argentina's long-term foreign currency debt rating to BB from BB-minus.

"We believe that the upgrading, in a way, was catching up with what was already being observed in international markets. These will consolidate the downward trend in interest rates, so we expect that to be important for investment in Argentina," Fernandez said.
Argentina Pars ended higher trading up 1/2 to 62-1/8 bid, Argentine Frbs also gained 1/4 to 89-5/8 bid.
Fernandez also said the Argentine economy was likely to grow faster than the original government forecast of five percent gross domestic product (GDP) growth for 1997.

In Peru, Marxist rebels continued to hold 72 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence marking the 111th day of the hostage siege. Tupac Amaru Reveloutionary Movement hostage-takers told Reuters there was no chance of resuming direct talks - on hold for three weeks - until the government showed the "political will" to address their demand for the release of jailed comrades.
President Alberto Fujimori said on Sunday that face-to-face talks would remain on hold until he was confident negotiations would bring real progress.
Peru PDI debt was quoted higher at 56-1/8 bid.
Among Eastern European credits, Bulgaria IAB bonds were up 1-1/8, erasing Friday's losses to trade at 58-3/8 bid. Russia dollar Vnesh also regained some ground to trade up at 77-1/8 bid.
